- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7–14 day window and reduce forecast slope.
- Model often underestimates true price in 1–3 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast for short-term bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be too optimistic when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing or reduce trend magnitude if sentiment swings >0.5.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model may be overfitting to recent noise; use 3–5 day moving average to filter out false signals.
